title: Rabbi Rechumai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in the Zohar, Introduction, 11a: Rabbi Pinchas was often before Rabbi Rechumai on the shore of the Sea of Gennesaret. Rabbi Rechumai was very old and his eyes were dim, and he said to Rabbi Pinchas: “Certainly I have heard that our colleague Yochai has a pearl, a precious stone, and I looked at the light of that pearl; it shines forth like the radiance of the sun… Go out, my son, go out; go after that pearl that illuminates the world, for the hour stands ready for you.”

Hyman also quotes the omissions to part I, at the locator ס״מו: “Rabbi Rechumai said: Glory and heart are one, except that glory is called after the higher [realm] and heart is called after the action below.”

notes.text: The omissions locator ס״מו remains literal rather than an established section 46. Its intended location and the second passage have not been verified in a named witness, so p002 stays held. The supplied first Zohar introduction locator and narrative remain separate.

Zohar I 11a in the consulted text has Rabbi Pinchas before Rabbi Rechumai by the Sea of Gennesaret and describes Rechumai as having lost his sight. Hyman describes his eyes as dim. The ellipsis in Hyman’s quotation skips the intervening description of light before Rechumai sends Pinchas to seek the jewel. The Soncino translation identifies the jewel in a footnote as Yochai’s son Shimon.

The earlier note on this passage predates the recovery of this source. The Or Breslev text of the omissions places this passage on 266a, section מו (46), and quotes the saying under the heading Sefer HaBahir. It cross-references Zohar, Tzav 33a. The consulted Sefer HaBahir §134 has a close parallel, with “action above” alongside “action below.” The supplied locator remains as written, and the exact edition Hyman used is uncertain.
